newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Anwar says ringgit not overvalued.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Anwar says ringgit not overvalued.

text.p: Malaysian Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Tuesday the ringgit was a victim of speculation and not overvalued.
"My firm view is that under the prevailing economic and financial conditions, the ringgit is not overvalued," he said at an Islamic capital market conference.
Anwar said that the Malaysian economy remained fundamentally sound due to long laid-down policies for balanced development and growth.
"In the immediate-term, however, volatility caused by speculative activity has put pressure on the ringgit," he said.
Anwar said this was a phenomenon experienced by all the countries which adapted a flexible exchange rate system.

"Not withstanding this, we would like to stress that whilst we remain committed to ensuring that the ringgit will not fall prey to speculative activity of the subversive kind, our policy of allowing market forces to determine the exchange rate remains unchanged.
"Therefore, we are confident that once the speculative activity subsides, the trend for the ringgit will reverse to reflect the underlying favourable fundamentals," he said.

Earlier on Tuesday, the ringgit slipped to a 33-month low of 2.5700 against the dollar as funds sold the Malaysian currency following Anwar's comment on Monday that the ringgit is within a reasonable range.
However, the ringgit recovered on Tuesday morning as funds started to take profits.
At 0200 GMT, the ringgit was trading at 2.5575 to a dollar.
